flashcards.q: What is the CRF partition function Z(x) and why does global normalization fix the label bias problem?
flashcards.a: Z(x) = Σ_y' exp(score(x,y')), summing over every possible tag sequence. Because normalization happens once over the whole sequence (not per-transition like an MEMM), no state is penalized just for having fewer outgoing transitions -- this is what fixes MEMM's label bias problem.

flashcards.q: How is Z(x) computed efficiently, and what's the complexity?
flashcards.a: Naive summation is O(T^n) (exponential). The forward algorithm computes it via dynamic programming in O(n*T^2), exploiting that the score decomposes into a sum of terms depending only on adjacent tag pairs.

flashcards.q: What does the Viterbi algorithm do in a CRF, and what's its complexity?
flashcards.a: Finds the single best-scoring legal tag sequence (not the full distribution) via dynamic programming, O(n*T^2). This is where a CRF's learned transition weights prevent illegal sequences like O directly followed by I-PER.

flashcards.q: What are the two halves of BiLSTM-CRF and what does each replace?
flashcards.a: BiLSTM (+ char-CNN/LSTM) is a learned feature extractor replacing hand-engineered features (word shape, gazetteers, suffixes). The CRF layer on top is unchanged from the classical formulation -- same global scoring and Viterbi decoding, just fed learned emissions.

flashcards.q: Why do many transformer NER systems drop the CRF layer, and when should you keep it?
flashcards.a: A strong pretrained encoder rarely produces illegal tag transitions on its own, so many systems use a simple per-token softmax. Keep the CRF layer when downstream logic needs a hard structural guarantee against illegal output (e.g. a booking pipeline that can't tolerate a malformed date span).

flashcards.q: What is the subword-to-word label alignment problem in transformer NER, and how is it handled?
flashcards.a: BPE/WordPiece splits one word into multiple subword tokens, but labels are defined per word. Standard fix: assign the label to the first subword token, mask the rest from the loss (or relabel with I- prefix). Getting this wrong silently corrupts training and shows up as inconsistent multi-subword entity extraction.

flashcards.q: BIO vs BIOES tagging: tag count and tradeoff?
flashcards.a: BIO: 2k+1 tags (Begin/Inside/Outside), compact, universal default. BIOES: 4k+1 tags, adds explicit End/Single tags -- measurably helps boundary detection on longer/adjacent entities, but larger and more confusable label space. Only switch if measured on your own data.

flashcards.q: Why is token-level F1 a misleading NER metric, and what's the correct alternative?
flashcards.a: Real corpora are 80-95%+ 'O' tokens, so a model predicting O for everything scores high token accuracy while extracting zero entities. Entity-level (span-exact-match) F1, computed via seqeval, requires exact start/end/type match with no partial credit.

flashcards.q: How much annotation cost does uncertainty sampling save versus random sampling for NER, per published clinical results?
flashcards.a: Roughly 66% fewer annotated sentences to reach the same target F-measure (clinical NER active learning studies). Uncertainty is measured via margin between top-1/top-2 Viterbi scores (CRF) or aggregated token entropy (softmax models).

flashcards.q: Why can't standard BIO/BIOES tagging represent nested entities (e.g. 'Seattle' inside 'Seattle-Tacoma International Airport')?
flashcards.a: BIO/BIOES assumes flat, non-overlapping spans by construction. Nested entities need schema redesign to avoid nesting, a layered extraction pass, or a nested-NER-specific architecture (span-based/hypergraph models).

flashcards.q: When does fine-tuned transformer NER beat zero-shot LLM extraction in production, and vice versa?
flashcards.a: Fine-tuned NER wins at high document volume (thousands/sec) where per-document cost/latency matters -- its cost per document is a small fraction of an LLM call's. Zero-shot LLM wins for new, rapidly-changing, or low-volume entity schemas where fine-tuning's engineering cost isn't justified.
